grammar.0.title: Letter names (approximate pronunciation)
grammar.0.text: A (ah) · B (bay) · C (tsay) · D (day) · E (ay) · F (eff) · G (gay) · H (hah) · I (ee) · J (yot) · K (kah) · L (ell) · M (emm) · N (enn) · O (oh) · P (pay) · Q (koo) · R (err) · S (ess) · T (tay) · U (oo) · V (fow) · W (vay) · X (iks) · Y (ewp-si-lon) · Z (tset). Tap each one and listen — hearing the exact sound is what matters.
grammar.1.title: Special letters: ä, ö, ü, ß
grammar.1.text: ä — close to the “e” in “bed” (Bär). ö — say “e” with rounded lips (schön). ü — say “ee” with rounded lips (Tschüss). ß — a sharp “s” (heißen); think of it as a “double s”. If your keyboard doesn't have them, you can write ae, oe, ue, ss.
grammar.2.title: Sounds to watch out for
grammar.2.text: w = “v” (Wasser, wohnen), v = “f” (Vater, viel), z = “ts” (Zahl, zehn), j = “y” (Jahr, ja), sch = “sh” (Schule), ch = a soft “kh/h” sound (ich), ei = “eye”, ie = a long “ee”, eu = “oy”. Most German words are read the way they are written.
